title: A login verified against a hash read before set-password could still rotate the session, and its rehash overwrote the new password
resolution: The rotation transaction rereads the principal and refuses the login unless it is enabled and still has the verified hash; tests change the password during the verification, with and without a rehash

title: A login rotated an anonymous session that had expired while the password was verified
resolution: The rotation transaction rereads the session and answers unauthenticated unless it is still live; a test expires it during the verification

title: submitTask checked the role on its run's project only after reading and validating the body, which section 2 allows only for createRun
resolution: A resource-project rule names where its project is; the server checks a path resource's project through authorizeResource before the body, and an HTTP test shows an invalid body does not precede the denial

title: The HTTP schema counts a login password before NFC, so a password set at 1024 characters after NFC can be refused at login in another form
resolution: Open: the fix accepts a body that Password.maxLength refuses as sent, a contract decision returned to the coordinator with options

title: An unknown login name verified at the current parameters, while a wrong password for a legacy hash cost only its weaker parameters
resolution: A failed verification lasts at least the last measured cost at the current parameters; a test with a costed fake shows equal costs for an unknown name and a current and a legacy hash

title: The request log kept every query parameter, so a password or an unprefixed session or CSRF token in the query was logged
resolution: Routes declare their document's query parameters and the log keeps only those, still redacted; unit and HTTP tests, a route check against the documents, and section 7 says so

title: The secret reader decoded each chunk alone, so a multibyte character split across chunks became replacement characters
resolution: A StringDecoder decodes across chunks; a test splits a line at every byte

title: Ctrl-C in raw mode ended the secret line as if confirmed, so set-password could store the partial password
resolution: Ctrl-C answers a cancelled failure after restoring the terminal mode, and set-password then writes nothing; a unit test and an integration test of hash, audit, and sessions
